title: The lift music played one floor too high 🛗

hook_text: At 1:33 in the morning the lift in my building played music and stopped at floor eleven. We only have ten.

scenes.narration: At 1:33 in the morning the lift in my building played music and stopped at floor eleven. We only have ten.
I pressed the button for my own floor. The display climbed past nine, past ten, and showed a number it should not be able to make. Eleven.
The doors opened onto a corridor I had never seen. Warm light. Soft carpet. A smell of fresh paint. At the far end, a door standing ajar.
I did not get out. The doors stayed open and the music grew louder. A slow tune, the sort people hum while they wait for somebody.
A man in a grey cardigan walked slowly down the corridor, holding a tray. He said, there you are, I was starting to worry. Your flat is ready.
I told him I lived on ten. He smiled. He said, nobody lives on ten. Ten is where we keep the people who are not ready yet to come upstairs.
I pressed the button for the ground floor, again and again. The doors began to close. The man put out his hand, gently, and held them open.
He said, take your time, we have all night. And the lift floor tilted, very slightly, as if the whole building was leaning towards me.
So tell me. Do you step out, or keep pressing the button?
